Spatial audio engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Spatial Audio capability in the binary covers storefront language. Xcode, audio pipelines, and Connect actually separate playback behavior from product-page copy:

  • AVAudioEngine & PHASE — configured in your app to render spatial mixes and head-tracked output. Controls whether immersive audio plays on supported devices. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • Dolby Atmos asset delivery — mix format, content catalog, and entitlement to stream Atmos tracks. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains spatial audio value to buyers.
  • In-app audio settings — Spatial Audio toggles, quality menus, and headphone-detection labels. Your listing may mention immersive sound; implementing audio routing is engineering work, not listing copy.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of spatial audio flags in the binary.

What China buyers still see when the zh-Hans row is incomplete

When Simplified Chinese metadata is missing or falls back to English, the China storefront product page mirrors your US spatial-audio marketing gaps:

  • English app name or subtitle — Search results and the product header show Latin script while competitors read native

Common mistakes on Spatial Audio zh-Hans listings

  • Leaving "Spatial Audio" untranslated — Apple markets 空间音频 in zh-Hans regions; English-only overlay lines on otherwise Chinese copy looks unfinished
  • Machine-translated "Dolby Atmos" as 杜比大气 — wrong term; use Apple's 杜比全景声 framing aligned with your content catalog
  • Claiming Atmos when content is stereo only — metadata must match delivery; do not promise 全景声 unless your mixes and playback path support it
  • Claiming head tracking without personalized spatial audio — 头部追踪 and 个性化空间音频 require the feature your binary actually ships
  • Conflating Spatial Audio with Spatial Persona — immersive headphone playback is not life-size FaceTime presence — different buyer stories on the product page
  • Calling any surround effect "3D sound" — align with Apple vocabulary (空间音频, 沉浸式音频) and your actual UX
  • Caption lines that describe US-only content catalogs — screenshot shows region-locked Atmos libraries but description never explains availability honestly
  • English-only What's New after a Spatial Audio launch — version notes are a separate field; base $79 focuses on evergreen listing fields unless you bundle What's New in intake
  • Assuming AVAudioEngine integration localizes the store page — engineering and App Store metadata are independent workstreams

FAQ

Does localizing my listing translate Spatial Audio controls inside the app?

No. AppLocale rewrites App Store Connect metadata — name, subtitle, keywords, description, and screenshot caption lines on your zh-Hans product page. In-app Spatial Audio toggles, Dolby Atmos badges in the player, and audio settings labels are binary or Xcode localization work outside AppLocale scope.

How is Spatial Audio listing copy different from Spatial Persona or SharePlay?

Spatial Audio is immersive playback through headphones or speakers — Dolby Atmos mixes, personalized spatial audio, head-tracked sound — not life-size FaceTime Spatial Persona presence, not SharePlay synchronized watching through GroupActivities. Screenshot captions should name 空间音频 or 杜比全景声 listening benefits rather than spatial FaceTime tiles or Watch Together overlays.

What character limits apply to zh-Hans Spatial Audio listing fields?

App name and subtitle are each up to 30 characters on the zh-Hans row. The keyword field allows up to 100 characters. Description and screenshot caption lines have longer limits but should stay concise — especially subtitle and overlay lines that must fit on-device mockups showing AirPods or immersive audio UI.

Should I claim Dolby Atmos or head tracking if my app only ships stereo?

No. Listing copy must match what your binary and content catalog actually support. If you output stereo only, zh-Hans description and screenshot captions should not promise 杜比全景声 or 头部追踪 unless your build delivers those formats. AppLocale rewrites from your English source claims; we do not invent Atmos or head-tracking support your app lacks.
